subject: ventures/restaurant-delivery-commission-analyzer
professional: a restaurant operator or restaurant-focused bookkeeper who reconciles third-party delivery payouts every month; they check first whether net cash ties to the bank deposit, whether error-charge reversals, adjustments and refunds net the right way, whether every fee column in the real DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub export is counted, and whether pickup and delivery orders (6% vs 15-30% commission) are separated

evidence.correctness: node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/2494317e-e49a-5e9d-81a1-ae5d701e315d/scratchpad/rdca/check.mjs /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/restaurant-delivery-commission-analyzer/calc.mjs. Against published rates: DoorDash pricing page (get.doordash.com/en-us/pricing, fetched 2026-11-13: Basic 15%, Plus 25%, Premier 30% of subtotal, pickup 6%, 'no payment processing fee'): a $40 Plus order gives take rate 25.00%, net 30.00, and at 30% food cost and $0.80 packaging net after 17.20 (hand: 40-10-12-0.8); a $30 pickup at 6% gives 6.00%; a $20 Premier order needs a 48.57% markup (hand: price 20(1+M), net 0.7*20(1+M) - 6 - 0.8 = in-store 14, so M = 20.8/14 - 1 = 0.485714). Uber Eats pricing page (merchants.ubereats.com/us/en/pricing, via WebFetch: Lite 20% Marketplace Fee): a 'Sales (excl. tax)' / 'Marketplace fee' sheet is read as Uber Eats at 20.00%. Stripe pricing page (2.9% + 30c): own-ordering net on $40 is 38.54 at Stripe's rate vs 38.50 at the tool's 3% + $0.30 default. All pass. Held at 2 because every amount goes through Math.abs (calc.mjs:208-209): a +$6 error-charge reversal is counted as a second $6 cost (errors 12.00, net 18.00 where the merchant actually kept 30.00), and a refund row with subtotal -15 / commission +3.75 adds $15 to food sales (gross 55.00 vs 25.00) and counts as a second order. The payout-gap finding does flag the first case (gap 12.00), but the headline take rate and net are wrong for any file with credits. Grubhub's fee page (get.grubhub.com/grubhub-pricing-and-fees/) could not be read (tables are images); no Grubhub rate was recomputed.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end on synthetic files: per-platform and per-order take rate, net cash, net after food cost and packaging, losing orders (worst ten), promo/ad return, weekday and daypart with the 5-order floor, markup needed, own-ordering comparison, payout reconciliation warning, cancelled handling, skipped rows with line and reason, UTF-16/semicolon/day-first input, multi-file load, CSV download (index.html:210-219). Served page https://marisstella.app/restaurant-delivery-commission-analyzer/ loads 200 (37,961 bytes) with the same calculator and an absolute canonical; served llms.txt points at marisstella.app. No TODOs. The README is candid that no real export was ever available, so the one thing a user actually does (drop in a real portal export) is untested.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/restaurant-delivery-commission-analyzer && node --test '*.test.mjs': 36 tests, 36 pass, 0 fail (116 ms); bare `node --test` as the README says also runs 36. Seven mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (ads dropped from charges calc.mjs:288, packaging dropped from markup calc.mjs:247, direct flat fee charged once calc.mjs:305, in-store base by (1-m) instead of /(1+m) calc.mjs:290); 3 survived (payout-gap threshold 1% -> 5% calc.mjs:406, lunch daypart end 14 -> 15 calc.mjs:219, take-rate high severity >= 0.3 -> > 0.3 calc.mjs:370). No test has a positive charge, a credit, a negative subtotal or a real-export fixture, so the sign defect above is invisible to the suite.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (447 lines, pure, no DOM), index.html module script (149-222), usage.mjs, both test files. Output is escaped (esc) wherever file text reaches innerHTML. Defects: the loss-order reduction is computed twice (calc.mjs:355-356); the variable `rented` (calc.mjs:287) is a leftover name from another engine; directOf charges the flat fee per completed order but applies the percentage to gross that includes cancelled-with-sales rows (calc.mjs:305); fee columns that match no alias are silently ignored with no 'unread column' notice (findColumns, calc.mjs:126-139); 'processing fee' lands in the column labelled 'Delivery / service'.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, independence clause naming DoorDash, Inc., Uber Technologies, Inc. and Grubhub, and DNT/GPC opt-out present and backed by usage.mjs (localStorage only, guarded). 'Column names are matched by alias from memory ... no real export was available' is stated on the page, FAQ, README and VENTURE.yaml: honest. 'Charges are read as costs whatever their sign in the file' (index.html:113) discloses the abs behaviour, though it does not warn that credits therefore inflate the rate. 'Defaults are typical card-processing figures' backed by Stripe's 2.9% + 30c. 'Reconciles' holds (test and check: platform rows sum to totals). 'Not modelled' list is fair. llms.txt source names the old github.io URL but the served file is rewritten to marisstella.app (source-only, not filed).
evidence.fitness: Walked the operator's monthly job: export last month from each portal, drop in, see which platform and which orders lose money, decide on a menu markup. On a clean synthetic sheet it does this well and the markup and promo-return framing is decision-useful. On a real export it is unproven: aliases are from memory; an Uber Eats file with separate processing or delivery-network fee columns (column names from my own recollection, not fetched) has those columns ignored silently (check 8: take rate 20.0% with two fee columns unread); adjustments and refunds inflate charges or sales; pickup and delivery orders are blended in one platform rate though DoorDash charges 6% vs 15-30%. A bookkeeper would have to re-check every figure against the deposit.
evidence.domain: Compared against the platforms' published plan structures (DoorDash and Uber Eats pricing pages, fetched) and normal delivery-margin practice. Right: effective rate over subtotal (the basis DoorDash states), food cost on the in-store price, markup as the price at which net equals in-store dollars, promo return as profit before spend per $1 in the best case, payout used only to reconcile. Departures: signed credits and refunds are not netted (calc.mjs:208); no split by fulfilment type (pickup 6% / 7% vs delivery) though both platforms price them differently; sales tax passed to the merchant and tips are left to an unexplained payout gap rather than read; no per-week fixed costs (DoorDash tablet $6/week) though the page lists subscriptions as not modelled.

defects.what: Every amount is passed through Math.abs, so credits count as costs and refunds as sales: a +$6 error-charge reversal doubles the error charge (net 18.00 instead of 30.00) and a refund row with subtotal -15 adds $15 of food sales and a second order (gross 55 vs 25). Take rate, net cash and losing-order counts are wrong for any export with adjustments or refunds; only the payout-gap warning hints at it.

Fee columns that match no alias are silently ignored with no 'unread column' notice, and the aliases are from memory with no real export; e.g. a sheet with 'Order Processing Fee' and 'Delivery Network Fee' (names from the auditor's recollection of Uber's report) reports 20.0% where the fees in the file make 27.0%.

Pickup and delivery orders are blended into one rate per platform though both platforms price them very differently (DoorDash pickup 6% vs 15-30% delivery; Uber Eats pickup 7%); there is no fulfilment-type column alias, so the per-platform rate and markup are an unexplained mix.

No test exercises a positive charge, a credit, a negative subtotal or a real-export fixture; the payout-gap threshold (1% -> 5%), the lunch boundary and the high-severity boundary can all be changed with 36 tests green.

Loss-order totals computed twice; `rented` leftover name; the own-ordering percentage is applied to gross that includes cancelled-with-sales rows while the flat fee uses completed orders only; 'processing fee' is filed under 'Delivery / service'.

verdict: On a clean sheet the arithmetic is right: a $40 DoorDash Plus order at the published 25% gives 25.0% and $17.20 after a 30% food cost and $0.80 packaging; pickup at 6%, Uber Eats Lite at 20%, the Premier markup (48.57%) and the own-ordering net at Stripe's 2.9% + 30c all match hand recomputation from the platforms' and Stripe's own pricing pages. The page is honest that its column aliases are from memory and carries the disclaimer and independence clause. It does not meet the bar. Every amount goes through Math.abs, so a reversal of an error charge is counted as a second charge and a refund row adds food sales and an order, which a bookkeeper reconciling a real month would hit at once; unrecognised fee columns are dropped without notice; pickup and delivery are blended; and three of seven seeded mutations, plus the sign bug, pass 36 green tests. Grubhub's published rates could not be read, so no Grubhub figure was recomputed. Correctness, verification, fitness and domain are 2; completeness, craft and claims 3.
